extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students in algebraic geometry (Math 216)
extracted.subtask_description: Exercises, definitions, and theorems about Kähler differentials, the relative cotangent sheaf, pullback/base-change/localization behavior of differentials, smoothness of schemes/varieties, Euler sequence, and birational invariants (geometric genus, canonical bundle, plurigenera).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of differentials (affine case)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A'←A and B'←B form a commutative diagram of rings, describe a natural homomorphism of A'-modules A' ⊗_A Ω_{A/B} → Ω_{A'/B'}. An important special case is B = B'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.2.K(a). In the tensor (co-Cartesian) case A' ≅ B' ⊗_B A one expects this map to be an isomorphism (see (b)); the construction is via the universal property of Ω and may be subtle depending on approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of differentials under base extension (affine case)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the diagram is a 'tensor diagram' (A' ≅ B' ⊗_B A, i.e., co-Cartesian), then the natural map A' ⊗_A Ω_{A/B} → Ω_{A'/B'} is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.2.K(b). The statement is the affine-case base-change property for Kähler differentials; the exercise warns the proof may be trickier than expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of differentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a ring map φ : B → A, multiplicative subsets S ⊂ A and T ⊂ B with φ(T) ⊂ S, the pullback map S^{-1}Ω_{A/B} → Ω_{S^{-1}A / T^{-1}B} is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.2.L. Intuitive picture: 'vertical cotangent vectors' are unaffected by localization. Important special case T = {1} or φ(T)=S; see Example 21.2.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentials of simple field extensions and separably generated extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Ω_{k(t)/k}. If K/k is separably generated by t1,...,tn (a transcendence basis with K/k(t1,...,tn) algebraic and separable), then Ω_{K/k} is a free K-module with basis dt1,...,dtn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.2.M. Hints: use the relative cotangent sequence (Theorem 21.2.9) to show the dti span, and prove linear independence by constructing a unique K-linear map sending dt1 to 1 and other dti to 0, treating finite generation first and passing to unions of finitely generated subextensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global (scheme) definition of relative cotangent sheaf Ω_{X/Y}
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism π : X → Y, define the relative cotangent sheaf Ω_{X/Y} as the conormal sheaf N^∨_{X/X×_Y X} of the diagonal embedding (δ : X → X×_Y X). The universal derivation d : O_X → Ω_{X/Y} is defined using the two projections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This globalizes the affine definition: on affines it agrees with earlier Ω_A/B, and for any open U the map Γ(U, O_X) → Γ(U, Ω_{X/Y}) interprets as 'taking the derivative' (21.2.20 and following).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine identification: Ω_{A/B} and I/I^2 (conormal identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Spec A → Spec B, the diagonal corresponds to an ideal I ⊂ A ⊗_B A, and there is a natural morphism Ω_{A/B} → I/I^2 induced by the universal property; this map is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem and proof in 21.2.22–21.2.24: check derivation properties and construct inverse g : I/I^2 → Ω_{A/B} by restriction of A ⊗_B Ω_{A/B} → Ω_{A/B}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative cotangent exact sequence for morphisms of schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Given morphisms X → Y → Z of schemes, there is an exact sequence of quasi-coherent sheaves on X: π^*Ω_{Y/Z} → Ω_{X/Z} → Ω_{X/Y} → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 21.2.25(a). This globalizes the analogous affine theorem (Theorem 21.2.9). Expect left-exactness under additional smoothness hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conormal exact sequence for a closed embedding of schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: If i : X ↪ Y is a closed embedding with conormal sheaf N^∨_{X/Y}, then there is an exact sequence of sheaves on X: N^∨_{X/Y} → i^*Ω_{Y/Z} → Ω_{X/Z} → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 21.2.25(b). This globalizes the affine conormal exact sequence; used widely for relating differentials under embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left-exactness of the relative cotangent sequence under smoothness
rubrics_metrics.description: If the maps f and g in the relative cotangent sequence are smooth, then the sequence is exact on the left (i.e., π^*Ω_{Y/Z} → Ω_{X/Z} is injective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.2.S. Hint: reduce to a block upper triangular Jacobian matrix argument (exercise 12.6.D was referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of differentials (schemes) and base change
rubrics_metrics.description: For a commutative diagram of schemes µ : X' → X over Y'→Y, there is a natural homomorphism µ^*Ω_{X/Y} → Ω_{X'/Y'}. If the diagram is Cartesian (X' ≅ X ×_Y Y') then µ^*Ω_{X/Y} → Ω_{X'/Y'} is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 21.2.27. Exercise 21.2.T asks to derive this from the affine Exercise 21.2.K by checking gluing; consequence: fibers of Ω are Ω of fibers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of fibers: Ω of a fiber equals fiber of Ω
rubrics_metrics.description: As a particular case of base change, the fiber of the sheaf of relative differentials is the sheaf of differentials of the fiber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement is asserted following Theorem 21.2.27(b): it justifies that Ω 'glues' the differentials on each fiber.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of smoothness via cotangent sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: A k-scheme X is k-smooth of dimension n if it is locally of finite type, of pure dimension n, and Ω_{X/k} is locally free of rank n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 21.3.1 (Redeﬁnition). This is the preferred robust definition used here; the dimension may be omitted when not needed. Connects to earlier Jacobian-based definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoothness can be checked affine-locally via Jacobian criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Smoothness can be checked on any affine cover by applying the Jacobian criterion on each affine open set in the cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important observation 21.3.2: practical method for checking smoothness by local computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoothness is insensitive to extension of base field
rubrics_metrics.description: Smoothness of a scheme over a field k is preserved (and reflected) under extension of the base field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.3.C asks to prove the converse to Exercise 12.2.F; this is a basic stability property of smoothness under base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: smoothness vs regularity at closed points over perfect fields
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is perfect and X is a finite type k-scheme, then X is smooth iff X is regular at all closed points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.3.D (IMPORTANT EXERCISE). Use base change to a separable extension and properties of regular local rings; this underlies equivalence used elsewhere (Theorem 12.2.10(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic smoothness of varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is an irreducible variety over a perfect field k of dimension n, there is a dense open subset U of X such that U is smooth of dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 21.3.5. Proof uses that the rank of Ω at the generic point is n and upper semi-continuity of rank of a coherent sheaf (Exercise 13.7.J), combined with separable generation of function fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left-exactness of conormal exact sequence for embeddings of smooth varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: For i : X ↪ Y a closed embedding of smooth k-varieties, the conormal exact sequence is exact on the left: 0 → N^∨_{X/Y} → i^*Ω_{Y/k} → Ω_{X/k} → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 21.3.8. Proof uses that smooth varieties are regular at closed points and that I/I^2 is locally free; reduces to checking at associated points and uses dimension-counting arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zariski cotangent space identification at separable closed points
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is a smooth k-variety and q is a closed point whose residue field is separable over k, then the conormal sequence for q ↪ Y yields an isomorphism of the Zariski cotangent space of Y at q with the fiber of Ω_{Y/k} at q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important Corollary 21.3.9. Use Theorem 21.3.8 with X = q and Ω_{q/k} = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric genus as h^0(C, Ω_{C/k}) for curves
rubrics_metrics.description: For a regular projective curve C over a field k, the geometric genus is h^0(C, Ω_{C/k}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 21.4.1. Ω_{C/k} is coherent so h^0 is finite. Exercise 21.4.C connects this to h^1(C, O_C) (arithmetic genus) via Serre duality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation for P^1: Ω_{P^1/k} ≅ O(-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For P^1_k, Ω_{P^1/k} is an invertible sheaf identified with O(-2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 21.4.2. Compute on standard two affine patches and check transformation of dx under x↦1/x; argument works over Z and base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentials on discrete valuation rings (DVRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A,m,k) is a DVR that is a localization of a finitely generated k-algebra and t is a uniformizer, then Ω_{A/k} is free of rank one generated by dt (Ω_{A/k} = A·dt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.4.D. Approach: show Ω_{A/k} finitely generated, construct a surjection onto Ω by σ(a)=(a−π(a))/t and use Nakayama to deduce principal generation; use reduction mod t^N to show no torsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler exact sequence for projective space
rubrics_metrics.description: For projective space P^n_A over a ring A, there is an exact sequence 0 → Ω_{P^n_A / A} → O_{P^n_A}(-1)^{⊕(n+1)} → O_{P^n_A} → 0 (the Euler exact sequence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 21.4.6 and the proof outline 21.4.7–21.4.8: construct the map φ sending (s_0,...,s_n) ↦ Σ x_i s_i, identify kernel with Ω by local computations on patches D(x_i), and check compatibility on overlaps (Exercise 21.4.F). Dualize to get the usual tangent bundle sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizations of the Euler sequence (projective bundles and Grassmannians)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Euler sequence generalizes when Spec A is replaced by any base scheme and further to projective bundles PV and to Grassmannians: e.g., for the Grassmannian G(m,n+1) one has Ω_{G(m,n+1)/k} ≅ Hom(Q,S) where S is the universal subbundle and Q the quotient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 21.4.9–21.4.10. Use universal bundles and the analogous O(-1) constructions; see Exercise 21.4.I for proofs and Exercise 21.4.H to check the projective-space case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical bundle and geometric genus for higher-dimension varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: For an n-dimensional smooth k-variety X, the canonical (line) bundle is det Ω_{X/k} = Ω^n_{X/k} (denoted K_X). The geometric genus is pg(X) = h^0(X, K_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 21.5.3. If X is projective (or proper) smooth, pg(X) is a birational invariant; Exercise 21.5.C connects geometric and arithmetic genus for curves via Serre duality (assuming dualizing property).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction formula for canonical bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is smooth and Z⊂X is a smooth subvariety, then K_Z ≅ (K_X ⊗ det N_{Z/X})|_Z; in codimension 1 this becomes K_Z ≅ (K_X ⊗ O_X(Z))|_Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.5.B. Hint: apply Exercise 13.5.H to Theorem 21.3.8. Useful in inductive computations for complete intersections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurigenera, Kodaira dimension, and birational invariance
rubrics_metrics.description: The j-th plurigenus is h^0(X, K_X^{⊗j}) and is a birational invariant. The Kodaira dimension κ(X) measures growth of plurigenera: the minimal k such that h^0(X, K_X^{⊗j}) / j^k is bounded; κ = -1 if all plurigenera vanish. X is of general type if κ(X)=dim X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 21.5.5 and Exercise 21.5.E. The Kodaira dimension existence and characterization via pluricanonical rational maps is nontrivial; plurigenera being birational invariants follows from pulling-back sections and Hartogs-type extension arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification examples: Fano, Calabi–Yau, general type via canonical bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: A smooth projective variety X is Fano if K_X^∨ ≅ O_X (or -K_X ample in other definitions), Calabi–Yau if K_X ≅ O_X, and of general type if Kodaira dimension equals dim X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 21.5.5 and Exercises 21.5.G–21.5.H. Use canonical bundle computations (e.g., for complete intersections) to decide class membership; Exercise 21.5.F shows K_X ample ⇒ general type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Birational invariance of H^0(X, Ω^i_{X/k})
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and X' are birational smooth projective k-varieties, then H^0(X, Ω^i_{X/k}) ≅ H^0(X', Ω^i_{X'/k}) for each i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.5.A. Strategy: restrict a birational map to its domain of definition (codimension ≥2 complement), pull back forms, and use Algebraic Hartogs (11.3.10) plus the locally free property of Ω^i to extend sections and show the pullback maps are inverse on dense opens.
